description: The League of Corinth, established by Philip II of Macedon in 337 BC after his victory at Chaeronea, was a federation that brought most of the Greek city-states under Macedonian hegemony. Its members formally pledged mutual peace, respect for each city’s existing laws, and collective military support, while Philip was recognized as hegemon and commander of a planned war against the Persian Empire. Although the league preserved a degree of local autonomy, it effectively ended the independence of the major Greek states in foreign policy and gave Macedon a legal and diplomatic framework for controlling Greece and mobilizing its resources for Alexander’s later campaigns.
